key_patterns.name: Heterogeneous risk perception
key_patterns.description: risk_perception varies across agents and is expected to be right-skewed with many moderate values and fewer extremes.
key_patterns.relevance: Directly informs individual adoption thresholds or baseline propensities; key driver of heterogeneity.

key_patterns.name: Layered, multiplex social structure
key_patterns.description: Agents have distinct family, work/school, and community ties with varying densities and likely directed edges that may need symmetrization.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific influence strengths and contact rates are necessary to reproduce realistic diffusion patterns and cascade sizes.

key_patterns.name: Demographic and occupational homophily
key_patterns.description: Contacts are more frequent within the same age_group and occupation, especially in family and work/school layers.
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily shapes local clustering and adoption clusters, affecting cascade propagation and subgroup adoption rates.

key_patterns.name: Temporal persistence (behavioral inertia)
key_patterns.description: wearing_mask status shows autocorrelation day-to-day; adopters often continue wearing masks the next day.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports inclusion of a persistence term or lower dropout probability to match observed stickiness and drop_rate.

key_patterns.name: Information exposure effect
key_patterns.description: received_info is associated with higher next-day adoption probabilities and short-term spikes in adoption.
key_patterns.relevance: Quantifies exogenous influence channel; needed for policy_effect_size and to separate peer vs external effects.

key_patterns.name: Early adopter clusters and cascades
key_patterns.description: Adopters tend to cluster in connected components; cascades originate in high-degree or highly clustered regions.
key_patterns.relevance: Calibration must match cascade_size_distribution and peak_adoption_rate, requiring correct peer influence strength and layer weights.

key_patterns.name: Degree heterogeneity and centrality
key_patterns.description: Community and work/school layers likely exhibit skewed degree distributions with potential hubs; family is tighter and smaller.
key_patterns.relevance: Central agents disproportionately contribute to diffusion; informs targeting strategies and R_behavior estimation.

key_distributions.name: Risk perception distribution
key_distributions.description: Fit a Beta distribution to risk_perception in the agent registry.

key_distributions.name: Degree distributions by layer
key_distributions.description: Empirical degree pmfs for family, work_school, community; consider in/out-degree if directed then symmetrize.
key_distributions.parameters: mean_degree_family, mean_degree_work, mean_degree_comm; variance per layer; tail index for community if heavy-tailed

key_distributions.name: Clustering and assortativity
key_distributions.description: Local clustering coefficients and assortativity by age_group and occupation per layer.

key_distributions.name: Adoption timing (survival/hazard)
key_distributions.description: Time-to-first-adoption among non-adopters at day 0; model as discrete-time hazard with covariates.
key_distributions.parameters: baseline_hazard (lambda0), hazard multipliers: HR_info, HR_peer_family, HR_peer_work, HR_peer_comm

key_distributions.name: Dropout (cessation) probability
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of switching from wearing_mask=1 to 0.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception increases adoption probability and decreases threshold.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate via logistic coefficient beta_risk > 0; strength medium to strong depending on variance

key_relationships.relationship: Exposure to information raises adoption probability within 1–2 days.
Proportion of neighbors wearing masks increases adoption probability; family influence strongest.
key_relationships.strength: beta_peer_family > beta_peer_work > beta_peer_comm; magnitudes to be estimated

key_relationships.relationship: More connected agents are more likely to receive info (if info diffuses socially) and to adopt earlier.
key_relationships.strength: Positive; quantify via regression of received_info on degree and layer counts

key_relationships.relationship: Subgroups with higher contact rates or higher risk_perception adopt earlier.
key_relationships.strength: Heterogeneous; measure via subgroup fixed effects

symmetrize_edges.notes: Reciprocity not guaranteed; symmetrize to model undirected social influence unless directional influence is intended.

layer_weights.source: Calibrated against train_data peer-effect coefficients by layer
layer_weights.notes: Initialize with these ratios; re-estimate so that beta_peer_family:beta_peer_work:beta_peer_comm ≈ observed ratios.

mixing_homophily.notes: Compute assortativity coefficients and ensure simulation preserves them.

degree_targets.notes: Use empirical means/variances as targets; preserve heavy tail if present in community.

time_step_days.notes: All hazards and probabilities are per day.

adoption_rule.source: Calibrated on train_data joined with network exposures
adoption_rule.notes: Pr(wear_t=1) = sigmoid(beta0 + beta_persist*wear_{t-1} + beta_info*info_t + sum_l beta_peer_l*peer_frac_{l,t-1} + beta_risk*risk_i + interactions).

beta0_intercept.notes: Intercept of logistic model without covariates.

beta_persist.notes: Captures inertia; should be positive and large if drop_rate is low.

beta_info.notes: Effect of exogenous information on same-day/next-day adoption; test lags 0–2.

beta_peer_by_layer.notes: Compute fraction of neighbors wearing at t-1 per layer and fit coefficients.

dropout_probability.notes: Compute overall and stratified by subgroup; use as per-day drop_rate.

noise_std.source: Fit residual variance from logistic GLMM
noise_std.notes: Accounts for unobserved heterogeneity; alternatively use agent random effects.

info_arrival_prob_base.notes: Baseline daily probability of exogenous info absent social diffusion.

social_info_boost.source: train_data.csv + Network JSON (neighbor info states if available, or proxy by peer adoption)
social_info_boost.notes: If modeling info diffusion separately, calibrate boost to info arrival from informed neighbors.

info_effect_half_life_days.source: Heuristic then calibrate to short-term adoption spikes post-info
info_effect_half_life_days.notes: Decay of info impact; tune to match transient increases in adoption.

threshold_rule.notes: theta_i = clamp(1 - alpha_risk * risk_perception_i, 0, 1); adopt if weighted peer_frac >= theta_i.

alpha_risk_to_threshold.source: Calibrate to match adoption_by_subgroup and overall diffusion_speed
alpha_risk_to_threshold.notes: Scales risk_perception into thresholds; cross-validate against logistic model mapping.

subgroup_contact_multipliers.source: Domain-informed prior; refine using degree by occupation from Network JSON
subgroup_contact_multipliers.notes: Adjust effective contact rate by occupation to reflect mixing intensity.

initial_adoption_rate.notes: Seed initial wearing states directly from data if simulating from day 0.

initial_info_rate.notes: Set baseline info exposure at start.

seeding_strategy_if_missing.notes: Seed top-k central nodes or high risk_perception agents to explore cascade sensitivity.

campaign_effect_size.source: train_data.csv (received_info as treated) + synthetic control in simulation
campaign_effect_size.notes: Difference-in-differences: compare adoption before/after info bursts vs similar agents without info.

mandate_threshold_shift.source: Policy scenario assumption; calibrate to observed jumps if any
mandate_threshold_shift.notes: Global shift in thresholds or intercept during mandate; tuned to match peak_adoption_rate changes.

influence_attribution_window_days.notes: Attribute a new adopter to neighbors who were adopters at t-1; expand to 2 days in sensitivity.

cascade_component_definition.value: Connected components among adopters in symmetrized graph
cascade_component_definition.notes: Measure size distribution per day and cumulatively.

R_behavior_estimation_method.notes: Estimate in early phase t where adoption_rate < 10% to avoid saturation.

preprocessing_steps.purpose: Ensure agent_id types match across CSV and JSON; validate all referenced neighbors exist.
Remove self-loops, deduplicate edges, and create undirected layers with weights.
For each agent-day, compute peer_frac_{family,work,community} at t-1 using train_data and network.
Cast wearing_mask and received_info to {0,1}; sort by (agent_id, day) and check for duplicate keys.
Impute missing day rows per agent (carry-forward states for exposures or mark as missing) to maintain regular timesteps.
Join age_group and occupation; compute degree, k-core, and betweenness (optional) for targeting and analysis.

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: Two-stage estimation with cross-checks: (1) Baseline and exogenous effects: Fit a discrete-time logistic model of wearing_mask_t on wearing_{t-1}, received_info_t, risk_perception, subgroup fixed effects (age_group, occupation). Estimate p_drop and persistence directly from transitions. (2) Peer effects and layer weights: Join network exposures (peer_frac by layer at t-1) and fit a GLMM with agent random intercepts to obtain beta_peer coefficients per layer and refine layer_weights. Use early-phase data to estimate R_behavior. If thresholds are used instead of logistic, map logistic coefficients to equivalent threshold parameters via matching adoption_rate_over_time. Final tuning: Use simulation-based calibration (grid or Bayesian optimization/ABC-SMC) to minimize discrepancy between simulated and empirical trajectories for adoption_rate_over_time, diffusion_speed, peak_adoption_rate, time_to_majority, and cascade_size_distribution.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Temporal holdout and posterior predictive checks: hold out the last 20% of days for validation. Validate that simulated adoption_rate_over_time tracks the holdout curve within tolerance bands, that final_adoption_rate and time_to_majority match observed values, and that cascade_size_distribution and adoption_by_subgroup are replicated. Compute R_behavior in early holdout days and compare. Conduct sensitivity analyses by perturbing risk_perception distribution parameters and layer_weights. For policy_effect_size, simulate counterfactuals by removing received_info and use DiD to ensure estimated effects align with empirical differences.

file_summaries:
- Overall data structure and type
  - CSV, flat tabular dataset; one row per agent (no nesting).
  - Columns: agent_id (integer, unique), age_group (categorical), occupation (categorical), risk_perception (float in [0,1]).
  - Intended as the primary agent registry; agent_id serves as primary key for joins with other files (e.g., network edges, locations).

- Meaning of keys or columns
  - agent_id: Unique identifier for each simulated individual.
  - age_group: Demographic segment (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age); can drive contact patterns, susceptibility, and policy targeting.
  - occupation: Social role/work context (e.g., Student, Blue Collar, White Collar); informs mixing layers (school, workplace) and contact rates.
  - risk_perception: Normalized propensity to perceive infection risk; higher values imply greater baseline likelihood of mask adoption and/or lower adoption thresholds.

- Relationships or nested elements
  - No nested structures or composite keys.
  - agent_id is the join key to external network/topology files and to time-varying state logs.
  - age_group and occupation imply homophily and multilayer contacts (household/school/work), but those layers are not encoded here.

- How this data should inform simulation entities or interactions
  - Initialize each agent’s attributes: demographics (age_group), role (occupation), and psychological parameter (risk_perception).
  - Behavior rules:
    - Baseline mask adoption probability seeded from risk_perception.
    - Adoption/update thresholds or susceptibility to peer influence modulated by risk_perception (e.g., higher risk_perception → lower threshold).
    - Influence weights and contact rates stratified by age_group/occupation (e.g., students cluster in school layer; blue/white collar in workplace layer).
  - Network construction:
    - Use age_group/occupation to shape homophily and layer membership; agent_id to link to edges.
  - Policy experiments:
    - Targeted interventions by demographic/occupation segment and sensitivity analyses by risk_perception distribution.

- Data structure and type: JSON object (dictionary) mapping agent IDs to adjacency lists; each value is an object with three arrays of integer IDs.
- Top-level keys: Stringified integer agent IDs (e.g., "0", "1"). Each corresponds to one simulated individual.
- Nested keys: "family", "work_school", "community" denote distinct social layers; values are lists of agent IDs representing that agent’s contacts in that layer.
- Element types: Contact lists are integer IDs; IDs refer to other agents present as top-level keys elsewhere in the file.
- Relationship semantics: Layered/multiplex network; edges are given from the perspective of the listed agent. Reciprocity is not guaranteed in the data, so edges may be directed unless you symmetrize.
- Cardinality/coverage: Each agent typically has entries for all three layers; lists may vary in length and could be empty; validate that all referenced IDs exist.
- Interpretation for simulation entities: 
  - Create one agent per top-level key.
  - Build three graphs (family, work/school, community) using the layer-specific adjacency lists.
  - Optionally merge into a single multiplex graph with layer tags or weights.
- Interaction modeling:
  - Use layer-specific contact rates/weights (e.g., family > work_school > community) to compute social influence on mask adoption.
  - Influence from neighbors should be aggregated per layer (e.g., weighted proportion wearing masks) and combined to update each agent’s behavior per timestep.
  - Decide on directed vs. undirected influence; if undirected behavior is intended, symmetrize edges.
- Initialization and dynamics:
  - Seed initial mask-wearing states per agent (random or targeted by layer/degree).
  - Keep network static (as provided) unless modeling churn; time dynamics occur in agent states, not topology, unless extended.
- Data validation needs:
  - Ensure all neighbor IDs exist; handle duplicates; decide behavior for self-links (should not occur); normalize string vs. int ID handling consistently.

Semantic metadata summary for train_data.csv (for mask-wearing diffusion simulation)

- Overall structure and type
  - Flat, tabular CSV in long/panel format.
  - Each row is the state of a single agent at a specific discrete time step (day).

- Columns and meanings
  - day (int): Discrete time index (0-based). Defines simulation timestep.
  - agent_id (int): Unique identifier for an agent. The same agent appears across multiple days.
  - wearing_mask (bool): Agent’s adoption state at that day (1 = wearing a mask).
  - received_info (bool): Indicator of information exposure about mask-wearing at that day (1 = received info). Clarify whether this is a same-day event or a cumulative “has ever received” flag.

- Relationships and structure
  - Primary key: (day, agent_id).
  - Temporal relationship: Rows for the same agent_id across consecutive days form a time series to observe state transitions.
  - No nested elements; purely flat.
  - No social network topology, demographics, or geography included—these must be provided or generated separately to simulate peer effects.

- Implications for simulation entities and interactions
  - Agents: Initialize each agent with attributes wearing_mask and received_info at day 0 (or earliest day available).
  - State transitions: Use day-to-day changes to estimate/calibrate:
    - Adoption: P(wearing_mask_t = 1 | wearing_mask_{t-1}, received_info_t, …).
    - Persistence/abandonment: P(wearing_mask_t = 0 | wearing_mask_{t-1} = 1, …).
    - Influence of information: Effect size of received_info on adoption probability.
  - Information diffusion: If a network is supplied, map received_info to exogenous shocks or infer parameters linking neighbor states to info receipt; otherwise treat received_info as an external input process.
  - Validation targets: Aggregate adoption curves per day and per cohort (by prior state, by info exposure) can be compared between simulation and data.
  - Data handling: Cast booleans to {0,1}, sort by (agent_id, day), check for duplicate (day, agent_id) rows, and handle missing days if any (carry-forward or explicit non-observation).
